title: Postmortem: Dedicated cluster capacity incident — noisy neighbors, reservation sizing, burst policy tuning
creator: Asha Patel
description: After a customer-facing latency spike on 2026-02-25 we ran a short incident response and identified multiple contributing factors in Dedicated: (1) noisy-tenant workloads saturated shared GPU queues on a subset of clusters, (2) several reserved capacity allocations were undersized relative to observed spiky request patterns, and (3) the burst policy allowed immediate large bursts that bypassed long-term fairness. This ticket captures the postmortem, concrete mitigations applied, and prioritized follow-ups for permanent fixes.
impact_summary: Between 2026-02-25 02:14 and 02:48 UTC, ~6% of hosted Dedicated requests served by cluster-prod-us-east-3 experienced elevated tail latency (p95->p99 increased by 3x) and a small number of timeouts. Two enterprise customers reported intermittent degraded throughput. No data loss. Escalated to Priority P1 due to SLO violations for dedicated customers.
timeline:
2026-02-25 02:14 UTC - On-call alert: sustained high GPU queue depth on node group cg-eus3-4.
2026-02-25 02:20 UTC - SRE triage: identified sudden increase in short-lived high-concurrency jobs from multiple tenants.
2026-02-25 02:30 UTC - Emergency mitigation: activated per-pool soft isolation (cgroup cpu/gpu share adjustment) and temporarily reduced burst cap for best-effort reservations.
2026-02-25 02:48 UTC - Latency returned to baseline after isolation and throttles.
2026-02-25 to 2026-02-27 - Post-incident investigation: gathered telemetry, reviewed reservation sizing history and burst token consumption logs.
root_causes:
1) Noisy neighbor effect: several tenants launched concurrent small-batch, high-concurrency workloads that starved the scheduling queues on a subset of GPUs. There was no short-window per-tenant GPU run-queue metric used in autoscaler decisions.
2) Reservation mis-sizing: reservation sizing heuristics used 30-day average sustained qps and did not account for short-duration diurnal spikes in these customers' workloads. Some reserved pools were consistently saturated during peak minutes.
3) Aggressive burst policy: the burst policy granted instant credits up to 5x baseline for short bursts which, combined with multiple tenants bursting simultaneously, caused transient overloads and head-of-line blocking.
4) Observability gaps: lack of a per-reservation tail-latency dashboard and missing alert on per-tenant GPU queue depth contributed to detection lag.
mitigations_done:
- Rolled out temporary per-pool cgroup adjustments to isolate noisy tenants (applied to clusters cg-eus3-*).
- Reduced default burst cap from 5x to 2x for best-effort reservations while we redesign burst algorithm.
- Applied short-lived token-bucket smoothing at the API gateway for affected customers to limit fanout spike.
- Created ad-hoc dashboard panels for per-reservation GPU run-queue depth and per-node GPU scheduler stalls.
action_items: AI-1: Implement per-reservation GPU run-queue metric (infra) — owner: Marco Ruiz — due: 2026-03-12 — add metric, expose to console, and create alert when p95 run-queue > threshold
AI-2: Revise reservation sizing algorithm to include 5- and 60-minute percentile windows in addition to 30-day avg (product + infra) — owner: Priya Menon — estimate: 3 — due: 2026-03-20
AI-3: Replace instant multiplier burst with credit-based burst smoothing: credits accrue slowly and cap consumption per minute (runtime) — owner: Daniel Cho — estimate: 5 — due: 2026-03-18
AI-4: Add fairness preemption policy to evict best-effort workloads when reserved pools approach saturation (runtime + scheduler) — owner: Elena Garcia — estimate: 3 — due: 2026-03-25
AI-5: Add per-tenant tail-latency dashboards and an SLA regression alert tied to reserved instances (observability) — owner: Kenji Tanaka — due: 2026-03-08
AI-6: Run two-week canary of new burst policy on low-traffic clusters before global rollout (release) — owner: Marco Ruiz — due: 2026-03-30
AI-7: Update onboarding guides and reservation sizing docs with recommended safety margins and traffic pattern checks (docs) — owner: Asha Patel — due: 2026-03-15
acceptance_criteria: Per-reservation run-queue metric present in console and alerts firing on test conditions
New reservation sizing algorithm evaluated on historical data and approved by PM
Burst smoothing implemented in runtime and validated under synthetic multi-tenant burst tests
Canary pass: two-week canary with no SLO regressions before global rollout
postmortem_notes: Trade-offs considered: immediately enforcing hard per-tenant GPU limits causes throughput loss for important bursty customers — chosen temporary fix favors soft isolation + burst cap reduction while building smoother long-term solution.
We evaluated hard isolation (per-tenant GPU device assignment) but deferred due to migration complexity and potential fragmentation of capacity for small customers.

Short-term reduction of burst cap will slightly increase tail latency for expected, small-scale bursts but reduces risk of cluster-wide head-of-line blocking. Communicated to impacted customers via account SEs.
retrospective_tasks: Schedule a cross-team design review for the new burst algorithm (runtime, infra, product) — target week 2026-03-08
Add monthly chaos test that simulates concurrent bursts from 10 tenants against a single node group
Include reservation sizing heuristics in the next pricing/sales checklist so Solutions Engineering can guide enterprise customers
status_updates: 2026-03-01: Implemented temporary burst cap reduction and per-pool cgroup adjustments; initial dashboards landed (Kenji).
2026-03-03: Completed metric instrumentation for per-reservation run-queue; alert thresholds draft under review (Marco).
2026-03-05: Design doc for credit-based burst smoothing posted to Confluence and requested review from runtime and infra teams (Daniel).
notes: Customer communication: account teams notified impacted customers with summary and timeline; premium customers offered temporary dedicated lanes if needed.
We will track 'time-to-detect' and target 50% reduction as a KPI for this initiative.
Estimated cost impact: minimal for short-term mitigations; long-term changes may affect pricing for reserved capacity and will be evaluated by finance.
